messages:
Avery King: Heads-up: Prospect (large payments provider) pushed back on our security questionnaire. Main asks: exact breach notification timeline, whether we can sign 72-hour contractual notice, evidence (SIG/CAIQ), and who handles regulator notifications.

Marco Silva: For SIG/CAIQ we can share a completed CAIQ snapshot + SOC2 summary under NDA. That's standard.

Eleni Papadopoulos: On notification timing: we differentiate confirmation vs detection. We can commit to notify "without undue delay" and aim to provide an initial customer notification within 72 hours of confirmed incident where practicable. We shouldn't promise to notify within 72 hours of detection because investigation may take longer to confirm.

Avery King: Prospect insists on the 72-hour clause with no qualifiers. Can we accept?

Marco Silva: Risky. Legal won't accept an absolute 72h promise because factors like third-party involvement, forensics, or law enforcement holds can delay disclosure. We can offer a constrained clause + an operational escalation SLA for Dedicated customers.

Eleni Papadopoulos: Suggested language for contracts: "Following confirmation of a Security Incident materially affecting Customer Data, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer with an initial notification describing the nature of the incident and known impacts within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation. Notification timing may be impacted by ongoing forensic activities or law enforcement directives; Redwood will inform Customer if such constraints apply."

Contracts Bot: Add bullet: "Initial notification will include severity level, affected systems, preliminary impact assessment, and named point of contact."

Marco Silva: For proof: attach a redacted IR runbook excerpt + tabletop cadence: annual company-wide + quarterly service drills for Dedicated. Include RCA timelines: preliminary findings within 14 business days; final RCA typically within 30-90 days depending on complexity.

Avery King: They also want to know which channels we use for notifications and whether we notify regulators.

Eleni Papadopoulos: Channels: primary = designated customer security contact email + account lead phone; secondary = customer portal advisory for Dedicated/Private. Regulator notifications: we do not proactively notify regulatory bodies on behalf of customers unless contractually authorized. We will provide all artifacts and reasonable assistance for customer regulatory filings.

Marco Silva: Also offer: for Enterprise/Dedicated customers we can include a 24x7 on-call contact and a Sev1 acknowledgement SLA (e.g., 1 hour). That often satisfies concerns about responsiveness.

Avery King: Good. Anything to help them accept the qualified 72h clause?

IR Ops: Recommend adding a transparency commitment: "Redwood will provide status updates at least every 24 hours for high-severity incidents until resolved or transitioned to post-incident reporting." This gives customers cadence and confidence.

Eleni Papadopoulos: Also call out differences for trial/POC orgs: limited operational guarantees, and incident comms may be routed via product support rather than dedicated security contacts.

Avery King: I'll draft the email: include CAIQ availability under NDA, the redacted runbook excerpt, the proposed contract clause, acknowledgement SLA for Dedicated, and the status-update commitment. Can someone review before I send?

Marco Silva: I'll take a pass in 20.

Contracts Bot: Templates linked: https://internal.redwood/contracts/ir-clauses (access: legal-sales).

Avery King: Thanks team — will circulate draft here in 30 mins.
